newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba hog price plan reinstated as packers talk.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba hog price plan reinstated as packers talk.

text.p: A hog pricing formula that expired last Friday was reinstated for two more weeks in the hope that packers and hog marketer Manitoba Pork can agree on a price scheme, Manitoba Agriculture Minister Harry Enns told reporters.
"They (Manitoba Pork) have indicated to the processors they will go back to the negotiating table, and for a two-week period the old pricing formula will be in effect," Enns said.
The dispute over hog pricing led to 206 layoffs Monday. Manitoba's largest packer planned to lay off employees Thursday if a price could not be agreed for slaughter hogs.
Manitoba sold 57,000 slaughter hogs a week in calendar 1996 and slaughtered 37,000 in the province. Provincial plant capacity stands at 48,000 hogs a week, Agriculture Canada statistics show.
Manitoba Pork used to set one price for all processors when it had a monopoly on sales. That monopoly was revoked by the provincial government on July 1, 1996.

The agency has since retained 80 to 85 percent of market share using a single price offered to all packers derived from the western U.S. Corn Belt hog value and deducting C$10 per 100 kg for freight to Winnipeg, Enns said. The scheme expired Friday.

Several packers refused to bid for hogs under the new scheme. They included Canada's largest food processor, Maple Leaf Foods Inc, which owns the Burns Meats hog plant in Winnipeg, along with Schneider Corp in Winnipeg and Springhill Farms at the Hutterite Colony in Neepawa.
Springhill recalled 90 employees on Thursday after the stopgap measure was announced, Enns said.
Only processor Jack Forgan Meats agreed to use the new formula, which resembles the Chicago Mercantile Exchange lean hogs index converted into Canadian dollars.
The contentious issue in the new formula was making the freight deduction optional in processor bids, Enns said.
Processors believed whoever was willing to absorb the entire C$10 per 100 kg deduction in their bid would receive the largest supply of hogs, industry analysts said.
